newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa falls prey to New York in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa falls prey to New York in dull trade.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures fell prey to weaker New York values on Thursday in an otherwise featureless pre-Easter market.
A slide in New York prompted arbitrage selling but volume was a meagre 4,871 lots and business consisted of book squaring and some trade long liquidation ahead of the long weekend.
LIFFE will be closed Good Friday and Easter Monday. Trading will resume on Tuesday.

Thursday's session got off to a slow start with prices edging a touch lower at midday, but received a hammering from New York in the afternoon, dashing hopes again for an assault on resistance seen initially around 1,035-40 basis May.
The benchmark May contract shed 13 stg to close at 1,017 stg per tonne. Its intra-day low was 1,012 stg.
"There was a bit of selling from Fimat, arbitrage I guess," said one trader.
Mees Pierson had sold about 100 lots of May earlier in the session, E.D.& F. Man had sold September and bought July while other sellers on the board included MHF Futures and Cargill, he said.
The latest weekly data on Ghana cocoa purchases went largely ignored as the West African main crop tapers off.
"The crop is finished. Nobody's interested," said the trader.

The Ghana Cocoa Board said 1,893 tonnes were purchased in the 21st week of the 1996/97 season ending March 6 with the cumulative reaching 296,109. This compares with 336,609 tonnes by March 7 last year.

While the main crop was largely discounted, prospects for the midcrops also improved with analysts in Ivory Coast now looking at a total of 150,000 tonnes or more after a week of prolonged thundershowers in cocoa areas, although more rain is needed in April.
"This should in turn enable a full year outcome of around 1.1 million tonnes to be achieved," said brokers GNI in a daily commentary.
But bulls have not given up just yet.
Sentiment may be given a fresh boost if first quarter cocoa grind figures due out in the first half of April come in line with expectations for a steady growth in consumption.
Traders are also closely monitoring the movements of Phibro, a major trade house believed to hold large physical stocks, for signs of a seasonal supply squeeze.
A key technical support level to watch is the chart gap between 989 and 982 stg. Failure to maintain this level may extend losses to 950.
